history.period: Visit of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, July 1673; Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji also visited
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Sikh gurdwara, keep-or-drop decision needed. This gurdwara at village Karhali, near Dakala in Patiala district, commemorates Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's halt here in July 1673 while travelling towards Delhi with 100 horse riders. A villager named Surmukh (also rendered Sanmukh), suffering from a contagious disease and living in a hut outside the village, was cured after bathing in a nearby pond at the Guru's behest; the Guru blessed that bathing in the pond for five Sundays would cure 18 types of diseases, and the site has a sarovar revered for healing powers. Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib also visited while travelling to Delhi. NOTE: the CSV name 'Gurudwara at Karhali' is generic; the shrine's proper name is per worldgurudwaras.com and DiscoverSikhism.

name: Gurdwara Sri Patshahi Chevin ate Nauvin Sahib, Karhali
town_description: Karhali is a village near Dakala in Patiala district, Punjab, in the Malwa region. It is a small rural settlement whose local identity is bound up with the healing-powers legend of its gurdwara sarovar. The nearest town is Dakala, and the district headquarters Patiala lies to the north. FLAG: CSV town 'Patiala' is the city/district; the actual village is Karhali near Dakala.
